newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben profits, sales rise ahead of float.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben profits, sales rise ahead of float.

text.p: German television group ProSieben Media AG, which plans to float on the Frankfurt stock exchange in July, said on Thursday that sales and profits grew in 1996 and through the first quarter of this year.

With just over a month before ProSieben's stock market debut -- the first by a German broadcaster -- growing profits enabled chief executive Georg Kofler to offer the prospect of generous dividends for investors.
Management at the company was made up of people "with a certain tendency towards generosity to shareholders", Kofler told a news conference called to announce 1996 results.
ProSieben Media AG, which runs the ProSieben and Kabel 1 commercial television channels, posted group sales of 1.69 billion marks ($996.6 million) last year, up from 1.47 billion marks.
Net profits jumped to 169 million marks from 96 million the year before, while group income from ordinary activities rose to 178 million marks from 111 million.
Kofler told reporters he expected both pre-tax earnings and sales to again show double-digit growth in percentage terms this year.
ProSieben ranks behind RTL and SAT1 as Germany's third largest commercial TV channel, attracting around one-tenth of the viewing public and a bigger share in advertising revenues.
Another indicator of the group's improved profitability was a rise last year in its pre-tax return on sales to 10 percent from 7.6 percent.
Earnings per share, based on the DVFA accounting standard used by German analysts, rose to around 3.10 marks in 1996 from 2.00 marks the year before, finance director Lothar Lanz said.
Earnings before tax and one-off factors were up to 5.60 marks per share from 3.50 marks, based on the 35 million shares due to be in circulation after the float, Lanz added.
Group sales rose 17.5 percent in the first quarter of this year to 479 million marks, while pre-tax profits rose to 84 million marks from 63 million a year earlier.
ProSieben Media AG is currently owned by Thomas Kirch, son of powerful Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch -- a champion of digital pay television in Germany -- and the Rewe retail group.
Kofler said a price range for the issue of 17.5 million preferred shares would be announced on June 23. An additional 17.5 million ordinary shares will continue to be held by Kirch and Rewe.
The preferred share offer is to be open to investors from the next day, with subscriptions closing on July 3. The first listing on the Frankfurt stock exchange is planned for July 7.
Banks will also have a "greenshoe option" to buy an additional 1.75 million shares if the issue is heavily subscribed.
Kofler said that the ProSieben dividend on preferred shares would be 0.15 marks above the payout for ordinary stock.
